stories.title: Orphaned, Rescued, and Rewilded, Female Gorilla Becomes a Mother in Historic Conservation Success
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: A female eastern lowland gorilla who was orphaned as a baby and later rescued and returned to the wild has just become a mother herself. She gave birth back in May in Virunga National Park in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the very forest she was reintroduced to years ago. Eastern lowland gorillas are critically endangered, so every new baby matters, but this one is extra special because it proves rewilding orphaned gorillas can actually lead to them thriving and raising families of their own. It's a hopeful sign for the whole species' future.
stories.why_good: It's a real, confirmed birth that shows a rescued, rewilded gorilla successfully living wild and reproducing, a milestone for an endangered species' conservation.

stories.title: Nonprofit Brings Free Music Education to More Than 20,000 Miami Students in 131 Schools
stories.label: people
stories.summary: A nonprofit in Miami-Dade County is now giving free music classes to about 21,000 students across 131 schools. For many kids, this is their only chance to learn an instrument or sing in a group, since school budgets often leave music out. Teachers say the program helps kids build confidence, make friends, and stay engaged in school. It's a lovely reminder of what communities can do when they decide every child deserves access to the arts.
stories.why_good: A real, already-operating program is demonstrably expanding access to music education for tens of thousands of children, with no political angle.

stories.title: Fighting Wildfires from Prison, A New Law Gives Ex-Cons Route to California Fire Dept. Jobs on Release
stories.label: government
stories.summary: For years, many California prisoners have fought wildfires as part of special crews, but once released, old rules kept them from becoming paid firefighters. California just signed a new law changing that, clearing the way for former inmates to join fire departments once they're free. It turns hard-won firefighting experience into a real career instead of a dead end. Thousands of people who already know how to do this dangerous, vital work now have a legitimate path forward. It's a second chance built on skills they already have.
stories.why_good: A real law was signed that measurably opens stable careers to formerly incarcerated people, helping both them and short-staffed fire departments.
